standard.title: Mathematical Modelling with Rational Numbers
standard.description: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems, involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts; formulate problems, choosing representations and efficient calculation strategies, using digital tools as appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying choices made about the representation
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply the four operations to rational numbers, work with percentages, and solve ratio problems (from AC9M7N06, AC9M7N08). Students have experience with mathematical modelling in prior years (from AC9M6N09).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students formulate, solve and interpret mathematical models involving rational numbers and percentages in practical contexts, justifying representation choices and communicating solutions in terms of the situation.

nodes.label: Formulating a model from a practical problem
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify the mathematical structure of a practical problem and choose an appropriate representation (fraction, decimal, percentage, or ratio) to model it.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a practical problem, identify what operation and representation are needed and set up the calculation.
nodes.typical_width: Identify when a problem requires a model rather than direct calculation; articulate assumptions made in setting up the model.
wider: Compare how different representations model the same situation (e.g. profit as percentage increase vs dollar value) and discuss what each makes visible.
Investigate how simplifying assumptions affect the model's accuracy.

response_modes.reason: Formulating a model is the step students most commonly skip, jumping to calculation. An explicit scaffold — identify known, unknown, relationship — is needed before students apply it spontaneously.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies the operation and representation needed for a given practical problem.
States any assumptions made in setting up the model.
Does not start calculating before identifying the model structure.

nodes.label: Solving and interpreting in context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students solve a mathematical model and interpret the result in terms of the original situation, checking reasonableness.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a modelled problem correctly and express the answer in contextually appropriate terms.
nodes.typical_width: Solve multi-step modelling problems in financial and proportional contexts; use digital tools where appropriate; verify reasonableness with estimation.
wider: Investigate financial modelling: simple budget scenarios involving income, expenses, profit and loss with percentage components.
Model proportion problems using First Nations Australians' contexts (land area proportions, resource allocation).

response_modes.reason: Interpretation in context is a distinct skill from calculation. Students who can compute correctly frequently give answers without units, in wrong form, or without checking reasonableness. Varied practical contexts build the habit of contextual interpretation.

success_criteria: Expresses the solution in contextually appropriate terms (correct units, reasonable precision).
Checks the reasonableness of the solution using estimation.
Does not present a raw number without contextual interpretation.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Financial modelling contexts (budgets, profit/loss, percentage components) offer advancing students rich multi-step modelling that integrates all rational number operations in a meaningful context.

nodes.label: Justifying representation choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students justify why they chose a particular representation and calculation strategy, and communicate this reasoning clearly.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain in words why they chose a particular representation (fraction, decimal, percentage) for a given problem.
nodes.typical_width: Compare two possible representations for the same problem, evaluate which is more efficient, and justify the choice.
wider: Critique a given solution that uses an inefficient or inappropriate representation — identify the problem and rewrite.
Investigate: when would a percentage model be misleading? (e.g. 50% increase then 50% decrease ≠ original value).

response_modes.reason: Justification draws on all prior number work simultaneously — representation choices, operation strategies, contextual meaning. The integration and articulation of these is the learning at this node.

success_criteria: Justifies representation choices with reference to the problem context and computation efficiency.
Communicates the solution process, not just the answer.
Can identify a more efficient representation when presented with an inefficient one.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Critiquing representation choices and identifying when percentage reasoning misleads (successive percentage changes) is a rich critical thinking task for advancing students within the Year 7 band.
